To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the global carbon cycle is out of balance and (2) that the global climate system may be out of control.

(i) the global mean temperature has risen by 0.74C over the past century, with most of the increase occurring in the past 30 years; (ii) the rate of warming over the past 50 years is nearly twice that for the past 100 years; and (iii) the observed rise in average temperatures, together with other phenomena, is extremely likely to have been caused by the observed increase in anthropogenic greenhouse gas concentrations.

(i) human activities have already had a discernible influence on climate, and are projected to substantially alter climate in the future; (ii) climate change will be accompanied by increases in climate variability; (iii) climate change will amplify existing climate risks and create new risks for natural and human systems.
